description_en: Threeśikharatemples originally part of apańcadevalacomplex and dating from approximately 14th-15th century.The monuments are found in the southern part of the Bhurtī Temple Complex. The site itself is located in the northern end of the settlement of Bhurtī, 3 km north of Narayana, the district headquarters. It currently comprises 22 standingśikharatemples (ordevala) and one stone fountain. Architectural activity at the site can be situated between the 13thand 15thcentury, a time period corresponding to the latter part of the Khaśa Malla empire and the early phase of the Rāskoṭi dynasty (Andolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 128-129,Sharma 1972: 23-31,Sharma 2012: 120-123).In 2008, the “Bhurti Temple Complex of Dailekh” was enlisted on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List by the Government of Nepal (criteriaiiandiv).The three monuments were originally part of apańcadevalaplan. Twośikharatemples were lost since the construction of the temples. This is attested by the organisation of the remaining temples and by a photo taken in 1967 by Marc Gaborieau, where a fourthśikharacan be seen west of the central temple. At the time, this now lost monument was already in a dilapidated state (most of the tower was missing).Thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which corresponds to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century. In the absence of epigraphic records it is possible to date the Bhurtī Pañcadevala 1 between the 14th and the 15th century.The sanctums are currently empty. Each of three temples was recently crowned by anāmalakaring, although it is traditionally surmounted by twoāmalakarings. According to local informants the work was supervised by the Department of Archaeology and executed by stone sculptors from Bhaktapur.
monument_assessment: Restored, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
